title: Best Time to Visit
description1: November to February offers the most pleasant weather with temperatures between 20-32°C. The monsoon season (June to September) brings lush green landscapes but some activities may be limited.
dscription2: October and March are transition months with fewer tourists and decent weather, making them ideal for budget travelers.
note: Avoid peak holiday seasons (Christmas, New Year) for better rates and fewer crowds.

title: Accommodation
description1: South Goa offers a range of accommodations from luxury resorts to budget guesthouses and beach huts. Book in advance during peak season (December-January).
dscription2: Palolem, Agonda, and Benaulim are ideal for budget travelers while Cavelossim and Mobor cater to luxury seekers.
description3: Consider homestays like ApnaGoa Homestays for an authentic experience with local hosts who can provide personalized recommendations.
note: Beachfront accommodations may be more expensive but offer convenience and stunning views.

title: Getting Around
description1: Rent a scooter (₹300-500/day) or motorbike for maximum flexibility - the best way to explore hidden beaches and villages.
description2: Auto-rickshaws and taxis are available but agree on fares before starting your journey. Consider Goa Miles app for metered taxi service.
description3: Public buses are economical but infrequent in South Goa. Private car rentals with drivers cost around ₹2,500-3,500/day.
note: Always wear helmets on two-wheelers and carry a valid driving license.

title: Shopping
description1: Pick up souvenirs like Goan spices, cashew nuts, handicrafts, shell items, and feni (local liquor). Anjuna Flea Market is famous for bohemian clothing and accessories.
dscription2: Local art, ceramics, and handmade jewelry can be found in boutiques around Palolem and Margao. Bargaining is expected at markets and street stalls.
description3: For authentic spices, visit the Margao or Mapusa market where locals shop.
note: Check cashew nut quality before purchase - they should be golden brown and crunchy..

title: Food & Dining
description1: Try authentic Goan cuisine including fish curry rice, xacuti, sorpotel, and bebinca dessert. Beach shacks offer fresh seafood at reasonable prices.
dscription2: Martin's Corner (Betalbatim), Fisherman's Wharf (Cavelossim), and Peninsula (Palolem) are highly recommended restaurants in South Goa.
description3: Explore local markets for fresh fruits, spices, and cashews. Wednesday Flea Market at Anjuna and Saturday Night Market at Arpora are worth visiting.
note: Drink bottled water and ensure seafood is fresh and well-cooked.

title: Safety & Etiquette
description1: South Goa is generally safe, but take standard precautions like securing valuables and avoiding isolated areas at night.
dscription2: Respect local customs and dress modestly when visiting religious sites. Ask permission before photographing locals or private property.
description3: Be aware of strong currents at some beaches - swim only in designated areas and heed warning flags.
note: Keep emergency numbers handy: Police: 100, Tourist Police: 1800-832-3224.
